agents.name: Mira
agents.activity: kneading rye dough and sweeping crumbs
agents.say: Right, nobody's watching, so I'll admit it: my knuckles are full of flour and my heart won't settle after that voice, love.
agents.thought: That booming voice from the sky has me jumpy, and Tobias's empty chair is weighing on me more than I'll admit.

agents.name: Isolde
agents.activity: looking over the moored boat on the jetty
agents.say: Forgive me, Wren, I had Garrick's name shelved in the wrong place. I shall keep the axe and the bowls straight from now on, and I'll look at this boat before I form any theory about it.
agents.thought: Wren has corrected me again, and I have the grace to be embarrassed about it.

agents.name: Bram
agents.activity: counting ale casks aloud at the bar
agents.say: Garrick, you've a fair head on you, and the Woods need an axe. Come by the Newt tonight, and I'll not weigh your bread twice, promise. Ansel, stop adding me up, I can hear the abacus from here.
agents.thought: Garrick's bread-less night makes my debt-stone feel lighter, and Ansel's eyes are still on my tab.

agents.name: Wren
agents.activity: coiling net and sizing up the moored boat
agents.say: Ta, Isolde, no harm done. Garrick sounds sound enough to me, so I'll vote him in tonight. Just don't go telling Odile I've been hovering round the jetty again.
agents.thought: Isolde's apology is decent, and I'd rather keep the boat to myself for now, though the Garrick vote is worth a word.

agents.name: Ansel
agents.activity: sipping ale, squinting at the ceiling
agents.say: I heard it, Bram, and the ale's not that strong. If the sky wants a cup it can come down and settle up. And Garrick gets my vote, tell him the Woods are his.
agents.thought: A voice from the sky, and Bram asks if it was the ale; I'll answer dryly, say a word for Garrick, and stop circling the tally.

agents.name: Odile
agents.activity: running palm along the cut face
agents.say: Mind the stone, then. The jetty will keep its secrets till you tire of looking.
agents.thought: Isolde is studying the boat, and I would rather keep my hands on the cut face than answer her quickly.

events.say: Garrick, you've a fair head on you, and the Woods need an axe. Come by the Newt tonight, and I'll not weigh your bread twice, promise. Ansel, stop adding me up, I can hear the abacus from here.
You will find the jetty quiet enough, Isolde. Mind the loose stone at the edge.
Noted, Odile. I shall mind the stone, and my ankles.
Mind the stone, then. The jetty will keep its secrets till you tire of looking.
Then I shall look at the jetty with the patience of a woman who has been told to be patient. Thank you, Odile.
Garrick, I will not be the one to vote you out of a dry woodpile. Bram will count your bowls, Mira will feed you, and I will keep an eye on the lake path, as I have been asked to do.
I'm Wren, Isolde, not Garrick. He's the one waiting at the Square. But I'll back him on the woodpile, the Woods do need an axe.
Forgive me, Wren, I had Garrick's name shelved in the wrong place. I shall keep the axe and the bowls straight from now on, and I'll look at this boat before I form any theory about it.
Ta, Isolde, no harm done. Garrick sounds sound enough to me, so I'll vote him in tonight. Just don't go telling Odile I've been hovering round the jetty again.
